attack_title: The attacks fool the model; random noise does not
attack_takeaway: The random-noise control fools 0 of 20 images; FGSM fools 90%, JSMA 85%, BIM and latent PGD 100%. FGSM, BIM and latent PGD share the budget ε = 8/255. JSMA changes only about 1,300 values (2% of pixels) but by large amounts, so its L∞ is 0.94. BIM, latent PGD and JSMA keep image SSIM near 0.9, FGSM 0.79.

qual_title.noise: Control: random noise leaves Grad-CAM unchanged
qual_title.fgsm: FGSM: the label flips, Grad-CAM weakens and shifts
qual_title.bim: BIM: confident wrong label, the evidence vanishes
qual_title.jsma: JSMA: the label flips but Grad-CAM barely moves
qual_title.latent: Latent PGD: Grad-CAM jumps to the background

noise: One example: a European fire salamander.
With random ±8/255 noise the model still says fire salamander (95%).
Grad-CAM and CAM keep their shape (SSIM 0.98) and SHAP 0.90.
LIME with its own superpixels drops to 0.31 only because the superpixels change; with the clean superpixels it stays at 0.90.
fgsm: Predicted: spotted salamander (41%), a close relative.
Grad-CAM and CAM weaken and slide off the head (SSIM 0.76 and 0.75).
The change is invisible at this scale (image SSIM 0.92).
bim: The map for the original class disappears (Grad-CAM SSIM 0.03): the network finds no evidence for the salamander any more.
jsma: Predicted: spotted salamander (54%) after changing a sparse set of values (the coloured dots).
A sparse attack can flip the label and spare the heat-map.
latent: Grad-CAM and CAM (SSIM 0.12 and 0.11) leave the animal and light up the lower corners.
The explanation now points at the background. Image SSIM 0.96.

ssim_title: Gradient maps resist weak attacks, not strong ones
ssim_takeaway: Mean explanation SSIM over 20 images (1 = unchanged).
Noise: Grad-CAM and CAM 0.96, SHAP 0.75, LIME 0.35 (0.74 with fixed superpixels).
FGSM and JSMA: Grad-CAM and CAM keep 0.73 and 0.88, well above LIME and SHAP.
BIM and latent PGD: every method falls to 0.25 to 0.40, and Grad-CAM loses its lead.
table_title: Three similarity measures tell the same story
stats_noise_title: Attacks move explanations more than noise does
stats_noise_takeaway: FGSM, BIM and latent PGD move Grad-CAM, CAM, SHAP and fixed-superpixel LIME significantly more than random noise of the same size (all p < 0.001). JSMA does too, with smaller effects (p ≤ 0.013). LIME with its own superpixels is already disturbed by noise alone (SSIM 0.35), so attacks add little there and only BIM is significant. Hypothesis H1 is supported.
stats_methods_title: Grad-CAM wins only against weak attacks
stats_methods_takeaway: Under FGSM and JSMA, Grad-CAM keeps its explanation significantly better than LIME (+0.41, +0.46), fixed-superpixel LIME (+0.30, +0.31) and SHAP (+0.22, +0.23), all p < 0.01. Under BIM and latent PGD no significant difference remains, and SHAP is nominally ahead. Grad-CAM and CAM do not differ (below 0.01), as expected on DenseNet. H2 holds only for weak or sparse attacks.
sweep_title: Explanation damage grows with attack strength
sweep_takeaway: BIM at ε = 1/255 is invisible (image SSIM 0.997) yet fools all 20 images and already lowers Grad-CAM SSIM to 0.65. At 16/255 it is 0.18. The label is fooled at every budget, so only the explanation shows a dose-response. H4 is supported.
supp_note: 20 images. All tables are in results/*.csv.
messages: FGSM, BIM, JSMA and latent PGD all change explanations significantly more than random noise of equal size (Grad-CAM, CAM, SHAP, fixed LIME; p < 0.015). Explanation damage is a real side effect of adversarial examples.
Against FGSM and JSMA, Grad-CAM and CAM keep their maps best (SSIM 0.73 and 0.88). Against BIM and latent PGD every method collapses to 0.25 to 0.40 and Grad-CAM loses its lead.
BIM, latent PGD and JSMA keep image SSIM near 0.9, yet Grad-CAM SSIM is 0.25, 0.29 and 0.88. Image similarity does not predict explanation stability. JSMA hurts LIME and SHAP more than Grad-CAM.
Damage grows steadily from ε = 1/255 to 16/255. LIME is unstable even without an attack (re-run SSIM 0.67, and 0.35 with new superpixels), so it needs fixed superpixels and a noise floor.
discussion_note: Differs from the earlier draft (Grad-CAM 0.91 under BIM, JSMA most damaging), which rested on two images. Here n = 20.
